impact.affected_asset: Availability of the consuming Node.js process or service.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a process that passes attacker-influenced strings to cross-spawn argument escaping to hang or consume CPU using a very large crafted string.
impact.security_effect: Regular-expression denial of service through excessive CPU consumption and possible process crash.

causal_trace.summary: A caller supplies a very large string consisting of many backslashes followed by a nonmatching trailing character to the argument escaping routine.

The pre-fix escaping expressions match a greedy backslash capture before a quote or end anchor, permitting JavaScript regular-expression backtracking on specially crafted input rather than bounded-progress escaping.
escapeArgument performs the two replace operations for backslash-plus-quote and backslash-plus-end-of-string handling; the PR reports that escaping a crafted large input hangs forever.
The reviewed advisory states that a crafted very large string can increase CPU usage and crash the program, producing availability impact.

failure.operation: JavaScript String.prototype.replace evaluation of the backslash escaping regular expressions in escapeArgument

primary_invariant.statement: Argument escaping must process runs of backslashes before a quote or string end without catastrophic JavaScript regexp backtracking on caller-controlled input.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The original replace patterns use a greedy backslash capture followed by a quote or end anchor; the maintainer identifies this as hanging on specially crafted input and replaces the patterns specifically to disable backtracking.

quality.review_notes: Primary patch and maintainer-supplied reproducer were inspected. The bundle contains no captured execution, timing threshold, CI result, or verified regression-test file, so the stated oracle is a proposed harness contract rather than an observed result. The advisory establishes package/version scope; exact deployment paths by which untrusted input reaches argument() are not established.

remediation.invariant_restored: The patched expressions replace the greedy capture-based patterns with lookahead/backreference forms intended by the maintainer to disable JavaScript backtracking while retaining backslash-doubling behavior; a subsequent commit corrects escaping behavior introduced by the first rewrite.

oracle.channel: Node.js execution of the maintainer reproducer
oracle.expected_negative: On a patched release, the escaping call should complete without the reported regexp-backtracking hang while producing the intended escaped argument.
oracle.expected_positive: On a vulnerable release, invoking argument on the supplied million-backslash-plus-trailing-character input hangs or causes sustained CPU use; the advisory additionally describes a possible program crash.
